cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description: Does the `--include` work with quotes as written? It's not detecting instances of the pattern for me when the quotes are present, but without the quotes, `--include=*.{py,pyx}`, it is detecting the pattern.  I'm stuck on the windows subsytem for linux at the moment though, so it could just be some weirdness with that.

evidence.attached_diff_hunk:
@@ -126,6 +126,10 @@ if [[ -z "$CHECK" || "$CHECK" == "patterns" ]]; then
     invgrep -r -E --include '*.py' "[[:space:]] pytest.raises" pandas/tests/
     RET=$(($RET + $?)) ; echo $MSG "DONE"
 
+    MSG='Check for python2-style file encodings' ; echo $MSG
+    invgrep -R --include="*.{py,pyx}" -E "# -\*- coding: utf-8 -\*-" pandas scripts
evidence.thread_resolution:

```sh
--include="*."{py,pyx}
--include=\*.{py,pyx}
```
